Master.g1.label: Request submitted

intake.submission_channels.summary: An entity with reasonable means available shall accept requests submitted by email and respond by email, unless the request seeks a response in another form.

intake.written_request_required.summary: The agency's five-business-day response duty is triggered by receipt of a written request for a record.

intake.form_permitted.summary: The Committee on Open Government develops a request form, made available on the internet, that the public may use to request a record.

denial.improper_request_denial.summary: A denial of access shall not be based solely on the category or type of the record.

Redaction.r1.label: Review against exemption / reason library

redaction.segregability.summary: Where electronic records mix accessible and withholdable items, the agency shall, whenever practicable and reasonable, design retrieval to permit segregation and retrieval of the accessible items to provide maximum public access.

Redaction.r1.city_config: The exemption library content (shared with Denial.nreason); segregability default applies in 25 states.

redaction.mandatory_pii.summary: An agency may delete identifying details when it makes records available to prevent an unwarranted invasion of personal privacy.

Redaction.r2.label: Apply redactions — mark visibly / note each
Redaction.r2.city_config: Marking style (visible box + exemption cite per redaction) — statutory content elements where present.

Redaction.d3.label: Legal review needed?
Redaction.d3.city_config: Legal-review escalation trigger for redactions — pure city policy (recommend: any novel exemption or protected-person class).

production.format_and_medium.summary: When an agency can retrieve or extract a record or data from a computer storage system with reasonable effort, it shall do so.
Where electronic retrieval/extraction requires less employee time than manual retrieval or redaction from non-electronic records, the agency shall retrieve or extract the record electronically.

production.no_medium_refusal.summary: An agency shall provide records in the medium requested if it can reasonably make the copy or have it made by engaging an outside professional service.

production.certified_copy.summary: Upon payment of, or offer to pay, the prescribed fee, the entity shall provide a copy of the record and, if requested, certify its correctness.
Where applicable, the entity shall certify that it does not possess the record or that the record cannot be found after a diligent search.

production.no_duty_to_create_or_convert.summary: An entity is not required to prepare any record it does not possess or maintain (except the statutorily specified subject-matter/vote records).
Records provided in a computer format shall not be encrypted.

eligibility.any_person.summary: Any member of the public may request access to the records of government; access is a public right exercisable by any person.

eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.authority: Matter of M. Farbman & Sons v. N.Y.C. Health & Hosps. Corp., 62 N.Y.2d 75 (1984); Committee on Open Government advisory opinions
eligibility.no_purpose_requirement.summary: A requester need not state a reason, need, good faith, or legitimate purpose to obtain accessible records.

eligibility.no_residency_requirement.authority: Committee on Open Government advisory opinions (construing N.Y. Pub. Off. Law art. 6)
eligibility.no_residency_requirement.summary: Accessible records are equally available to any person regardless of residency, citizenship, or status; an agency may not condition access on proof of residency or identity.

Estimate-Fee.proc.note: Collect-at-end is the default path wherever production is NOT statutorily conditioned on prepayment.

response.initial_decision_window.summary: Within five business days of receipt of a written request, the agency shall grant access, deny the request in writing, or furnish a written acknowledgement of receipt with an approximate date.
response.initial_decision_window.clock_spec: 5 business-days from receipt of written request

response.initial_decision_window.summary: A written acknowledgement must state an approximate date, reasonable under the circumstances, when the request will be granted or denied.
response.initial_decision_window.clock_spec: undefined-soft: "reasonable under the circumstances" from date of acknowledgement

denial.deemed_denial_on_nonresponse.summary: An agency's failure to conform to the subdivision-three response provisions constitutes a denial of the request.
denial.deemed_denial_on_nonresponse.clock_spec: on lapse of the § 89(3) response obligations

production.completion_window.summary: If the agency grants a request but circumstances prevent disclosure within twenty business days from the acknowledgement, it must act (state reasons and a date certain).

fee.copy_rate_per_page.summary: Fees for paper copies shall not exceed 25 cents per photocopy not exceeding 9 by 14 inches, unless a different fee is prescribed by statute.

fee.labor_charge.summary: Actual reproduction cost may include only the hourly salary attributed to the lowest-paid agency employee who has the necessary skill to prepare the copy.
No preparation fee may be charged unless at least two hours of agency employee time is needed to prepare the copy.

fee.actual_cost_basis.summary: For records other than 9x14 paper photocopies, the fee shall not exceed the actual cost of reproduction determined under § 87(1)(c).

The actual cost of engaging an outside professional service to prepare a copy may be included only when the agency's information technology equipment is inadequate to prepare the copy and the service is used.

fee.no_charge_categories.summary: Where an identical record was prepared for a prior request within the past six months and an electronic copy is available, the agency shall charge no fee except the actual cost of a storage device/media if provided.
Preparing a copy shall not include search time or administrative costs; these may not be charged to the requester.
